core_obligations: Choose a surjection R[x_1, ..., x_n] -> A and a presentation A' = A[y_1, ..., y_m]/(g_1, ..., g_l) witnessing that A -> A' is of finite presentation (proof lines 21081-21082).
Lift each relation g_i to an element g'_i of R[x_1, ..., x_n, y_1, ..., y_m] (proof line 21083).
Take the presentation R[x_1, ..., x_n]^{oplus s} -> R[x_1, ..., x_n]^{oplus t} -> M -> 0 given by the matrix (h_ij) (proof lines 21084-21089).

Assemble the presentation matrix for M tensor_A A': first t x s block h_ij, followed by l blocks of size t x t equal to g'_i I_t, and conclude that the resulting sequence with s + l t generators presents M tensor_A A' over R[x_1, ..., x_n, y_1, ..., y_m] (proof lines 21090-21098).
difficulty_reason: The lemma assumes a finite type ring map R -> A, an A-module M finitely presented relative to R, and a ring map A -> A' of finite presentation, and concludes that the A'-module M tensor_A A' is finitely presented relative to R (source lines 21072-21078). Unlike the base change lemma, the extension A -> A' is no longer arbitrary: the proof must choose an explicit presentation A' = A[y_1, ..., y_m]/(g_1, ..., g_l) (proof lines 21081-21082), lift the relations g_i to elements g'_i of R[x_1, ..., x_n, y_1, ..., y_m] (proof line 21083), and then build a presentation matrix with a first t x s block given by the original relation matrix h_ij followed by l blocks g'_i I_t, giving s + l t generators (proof lines 21084-21098). Recognising that this block matrix presents M tensor_A A' is the substantive step, and the author supplies no verification of it.
